author: benefits_content
readerQuestion: How are ACA subsidies calculated? [PAA 0/0; ac 6/6 on-topic, calculation and income-basis questions]
decisionGap: Coverage lookup returns no ACA subsidy-calculation page. /guides/how-to-budget-with-irregular-income/ explains budgeting insurance costs, not federal-credit math. Same-run ACA/Medicaid comparison defines the programs and application paths, not the personalized figure. No prior exact-slug source/history at local/pinned published revisions.
finding: Calculated sensitivity to income and premium caps, not a product test: a two-person household at$50,000 annual MAGI with illustrative$600 benchmark and$550 eligible plan premium has$268.85 monthly federal credit and$281.15 net premium, assuming all other conditions. At400%FPL=$86,560, illustrative$1,000 benchmark produces$262.80 credit; $1 above removes the ordinary modeled federal credit. Explain our arithmetic beside the inputs and avoid a claim that an income threshold alone establishes eligibility.
conditions: Client-side React island; inputs 2027 coverage fixed, household1–8, annual household MAGI, non-tobacco benchmark monthly premium, chosen eligible enrollment premium, and nonfinancial eligibility confirmation/unknown state. No ZIP database or fabricated premiums. 2026 FPL [15960,21640,27320,33000,38680,44360,50040,55720];2027 percentage bands <133:2.15%;133–150:3.23–4.30%;150–200:4.30–6.78%;200–250:6.78–8.66%;250–300:8.66–10.22%;300–400:10.22%. Linear interpolation within bands, monthly contribution=MAGI×rate/12, credit=min(enrollment premium,max(0,benchmark−contribution)). At<100/>400 or unknown/excluded eligibility show scoped explanation instead of approval. Benchmark excludes tobacco rating; IRSQ26 permits actual smoker enrollment premium for cap. Federal credit only, no state subsidy/cost-sharing estimate. Copy/download figures with conditions. Test boundaries, rate steps, blank/negative/huge inputs, caps and zero premium.
whatWouldChange: Federal-credit math requires a benchmark premium and correct annual MAGI, not take-home pay alone. Compare income scenarios before budgeting, update the Marketplace when income changes, and use its application for eligibility and exact prices. Employer/government eligibility, changed law or plan figures can reverse the result.
